challengeResponses.response: The source establishes eligible-target interception, not observed disruption or screen-reader behavior. Native-control exemptions answer a different question. Visibility alone would leave page reading beside a visible player exposed. I endorse reproducing the contexts, then removing shortcuts or limiting retained shortcuts to an explained, deliberate player interaction. Preserve the corrected gallery focus handoff.

The grouped native selector provides a structurally efficient route, but the supplied probe did not establish successful physical option selection. Angry remaining selected is inconclusive and does not establish a defect. Actually open, navigate and commit a nonadjacent option before deciding whether remediation is needed; verify the resulting value, heading, status and focus.

Single-theme viewing is an experiment, not an inferred improvement or required default. Measure the actual character size under the fixed mobile stage height before describing enlargement. Separately observe control discovery and unlabeled expression interpretation. Neither outcome establishes attachment or delayed recall; preserve anatomy regardless.

jointRecommendation: Endorse the proposed sequence: bounded keyboard evidence and correction first; native interaction, assistive speech, reflow and preference checks next; newcomer/revisit mobile comparison afterward. Creative alternatives may be explored without a demonstrated failure, while adoption needs a named benefit. Existing finite, quiet and opt-in behavior should remain the control.
nonblockingLimits: Shortcut context remains an implementation issue to resolve, not a defect already fixed by this agreement.
Native key selection, assistive output and mobile expression recognition remain unproven rather than presumed broken.
No numerical score is awarded or raised; this endorses work and acceptance criteria only.
